Shannon entropy maps

Source: R/entropy-maps.R
entropy_map.Rd

Estimates, at every pixel, the parameters of a SAR/PolSAR model with the observations inside a square moving window and returns the map of Shannon entropies (Ferreira and Nascimento, 2020; Nascimento, Ferreira and Frery, 2023). Optionally, the map of asymptotic variances of the entropy estimators is returned as well.

Usage

entropy_map(
  image,
  model = c("gamma", "g0i", "ggamma", "wishart", "g0p"),
  window = 7,
  L = NULL,
  channels = NULL,
  variance = FALSE
)

Arguments

image

A SARImage or an array accepted by SARImage$new().

model

One of "gamma", "g0i", "ggamma" (intensity models, applied to each channel) or "wishart", "g0p" (matrix models, for PolSAR images).

window

Odd side of the moving window.

L

Known number of looks. If NULL (default) it is estimated in every window.

channels

Channels used by intensity models (default: all).

variance

Also return the variance map?

Value

A matrix (one channel or matrix model) or an array nrow x ncol x channels of entropies. If variance = TRUE, a list with elements entropy, variance and n (window sizes).

Details

For the Gamma and Wishart models the computations are fully vectorised (local sufficient statistics are obtained from integral images), so the maps are computed in a fraction of a second. The G0I, generalized Gamma and G0 polarimetric models require a numerical maximisation per pixel and are therefore slower (use small images or crops to explore them).

References

Ferreira, J. A. and Nascimento, A. D. C. (2020). Shannon entropy for the G0I model: a new segmentation approach. IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing, 13, 2547–2553. doi:10.1109/JSTARS.2020.2997666

Nascimento, A. D. C., Ferreira, J. A. and Frery, A. C. (2023). Unsupervised segmentation of PolSAR data with complex Wishart and G0m distributions and Shannon entropy. Statistics and Computing, 33, 129. doi:10.1007/s11222-023-10298-0

Examples

img <- SARImage$new(SanFrancisco150)
H <- entropy_map(img, model = "wishart", window = 7, L = 4)
dim(H)
#> [1] 150 150
plot_map(H, main = "Wishart entropy")


Hg <- entropy_map(img, model = "gamma", window = 7, channels = "HV")
# \donttest{
small <- img$crop(1:15, 1:15)
Hi <- entropy_map(small, model = "g0i", window = 5, L = 4, channels = 1)
# }
